items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: I had a quintet who opened up for people like Pat Metheny and Buddy Rich.

ctx.x: You know? And I said okay, accounting and mathematics, I’m no good at that, what else, oh jeez. You know, but there would be the piano over in the corner and I’d think okay I’ll play for five minutes. Four hours later I was still playing. I managed to get decent enough grades and I thought I’m going to be a piano player the rest of my life, as I warned my mother at age three — “I’m going to be a piano player and this is what I’m going to pursue.” But no the jazz academic route is something that I missed entirely.…
So you just learned about voicing and ranges and all that from listening and talking to the players?
